title.narrative: Output A.1. More accurate and sustainable statistics on decent work using the latest statistical standards

description.narrative: Since early 2020, the General Statistics Office (GSO) under the Ministry of Planning and Investment (GSO) has produced increasingly high-quality quarterly reports on the Impact of the Covid-19 on the labour market. - Since these reports now integrate a focus on gender gaps and on informality, they have contributed significantly to draw policy attention to these issues. - These quarterly reports have become an important resource for Viet Nam policymakers, media, academy, and development organizations in Viet Nam for designing, implementing, and monitoring the responses to the outbreak of the Covid-19. - ILO report on the impact of COVID-19 on gender triggered an inclusive dialogue on this issue, made possible by the availability of new data from the integrated ICLS 19 standards in the LFS. - The sampling of the Labour Force Survey is substantially changed for better representativeness of the labour statistics. - The ICLS19 was officially applied in the 2021 Labour Force Survey and adopted in GSO formal quarterly reports. - In 2020, the GSO institutionalized the Viet Nam Standard Classification of Occupations (VSCO), through a Prime Minister Decision. This is an effort to standardize the classification of occupation not only in the statistical systems but also in all relevant work of other ministries. This standard classification was developed based on the ISCO-08 of the ILO and with technical support from the ILO. -Two significant changes related to labour statistics introduced in the draft law, including the inclusion of the measurement of informal employment into the Law and the adjustment of the definition of unemployment. - Thanks to the coming into force of the new VSCO developed with technical assistance from the ILO, the PES network of Viet Nam continued improving job seekers and job vacancies database to support for the job matching and labour market analysis functions of MOLISA. - The revised law on statistics, recently adopted by the National In response to the need for immediate and reliable data on the impact of the Covid-19 on the labour market of Viet Nam for better policy- making, from quarter 2/2020, ILO has been supporting quarterly studies on the impact of COVID on the labour market. - ILO has progressively built the capacity of the GSO on how to produce such reports, structure them etc. Then, ILO supported GSO strengthen capacity on enhancing the focus on women's disadvantage, and on informal workers. Finally, ILO have established a dialogue with MOLISA to strengthen their participation in the formulation of these reports, especially on the preparation of policy recommendations. - ILO published one analytical report on the impact of COVID-19, from a gender angle. This was possible thanks to the new data from the GSO that integrates ICLS-19 standards. -ILO continued to support the GSO to improve the alignment of the LFS with integrational standards. - ILO provided support to the MOLISA and the General Statistics Office (GSO) to develop a Viet Nam-specific version of the ISCO-08 of the ILO. - In 2020, the GSO started the revision of the 2015 Statistical Law in order to better reflect the SDGs monitoring. With technical support from ILO, GSO made remarkable development in labour statistics. -ILO worked with GSO and MOLISA to include important SDG indicators into the above revisions. - In 2020, ILO continued supporting MOLISA to improve the public employment services as part of C.88 execution. - ILO played key role in bridging related stakeholders (GSO and Institute of Labour Science and Social Affairs) to support the above works. - In the last two years, ILO has taken the lead to advocate for recognizing the informal employment in Viet Nam, and it has provided significant technical advice to our constituents and key stakeholders aiming at enhanced awareness and achieving a common understanding of the informality and policy implications in Vietnam; Provided technical input/note to th

title.narrative: A.1.1. Number of member States that strengthen their labour market statistics, standards and information systems through improved statistical surveys and use of other statistical sources
Output 5.1. Increased capacity of the ILO constituents to identify current skills mismatches and anticipate future skill needs

description.narrative: The Directorate of Vocational Education and Training of the Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs (MOLISA) has successfully applied the ILO methodologies to produce a national skills anticipation report and to make skills anticipation become an important chapter in the draft final National Strategy on Vocational Education and Training and Skills. The ILO, with supports from the Russian Federation and Sweden, and with RBSA resources, provided technical guidance in the form of terms of reference and helped the national expert team throughout the preparation and final production of the draft national strategy on VET, in which skills anticipation became a building block.

description.narrative: The Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs (MOLISA) promulgated decision no.773 for an action plan to implement the Government 's programme to support the labour market development until 2030. The ILO, with support from the Swedish cooperation and RBSA resources, provided technical advice forthe development of the national labourmarket development action plan and for the decision to implement it nationwide.
